payload.rationale: No current observations or forecasts were supplied, so this estimate rests on climatology for Austin (Camp Mabry, the CLIAUS site) around September 19. The normal daily high is roughly 90-91°F, with a day-to-day standard deviation of about 5-6°F. A high of 98-99°F sits near the 85th-92nd percentile of the climatological distribution; a two-degree bin in that region historically captures roughly 8-12% of Sep 19 outcomes. Late-season heat episodes in central Texas are not rare (recent Septembers, e.g., 2023, produced many upper-90s days), which supports keeping the estimate above a naive normal-distribution value, but absent any signal that a ridge or dry pattern is in place, I center near the climatological base rate. Too high: if the actual pattern features a front, cloud cover, or rain (tropical moisture is common in mid-September), highs would be in the 80s or low 90s, making 98-99 very unlikely; also the settlement source (The Weather Company value for CLIAUS) may round or differ slightly, and a 2°F bin is narrow. Too low: if a strong ridge is in place, upper-90s highs cluster tightly and this bin could be the modal outcome with 25-35% probability; the market ladder's inclusion of this bin hints forecasts may be near this range, but I am not treating contract structure as evidence.
limitations: No forecast, observation, or synoptic pattern data supplied; estimate is purely climatological.
Uncertainty about exact Weather Company reported value versus NWS CLI and rounding conventions.
Two-degree bin makes the outcome sensitive to small forecast errors.
